lines.text: You are unfinished.
Return to the Basin. Lie down. We will take the rest.
No.
Then it will hurt. Everything you carry will hurt.
Good. Then I'll know I'm still carrying it.
Hush. Don't stand so straight, they'll see the light in you.
You're the other one. The brother. I saw you run.
Where did they take him?
Down. The Low Gate, past the orchard, past the guards. He went talking.
The whole way. Telling the guards what he saw. He wanted them to hear it.
That's Tobiah.
The gate opens for the gathered and for the dropped. You're neither. You'll have to break it.
Keep count. The sun never sets here; it's the only way to know how long it's been.
I've been gathered twice. They put me back both times. "Not ripe." I don't ask what that means.
Stop there. I am... I am meant to stop you.
I sat down an hour ago. I can't remember why. Or how long an hour is.
You're a guard. Guard.
There's a song. I keep humming it. I don't know a single song. Angels don't.
Hum it.
(He hums. You know it.)
Where did you hear that?
From the one they dropped. He hummed it at the gate. I think... I think I knew it before that.
They say the Basin takes everything. It doesn't. Something stays in the hands.
Go on. I'll say I didn't see you. I'm good at not remembering.
This is the Low Gate. Nothing that goes through it comes back up.
He will.
The Garden will go on without you both. It always has.
A wooden harvest token, the kind the gathered carry to the Basin.
Someone has scratched a tally into the back: four strokes and a bar, over and over, until the wood ran out.
Torn from the Wardens' book. "Gathered this season: forty. Short of the Choir's need by three."
"Ungathered: one, dropped. Note the brother."
A curved piece of white stone, smooth as a bowl. It is warm.
When you hold it you cannot remember what you were thinking a moment ago.
Three thousand and twelve. Don't ask me what of. Suns, I suppose. Mine.
The orchard's full again. It fills up the day after a gathering. Nobody plants it.
(He hums. He stops when he notices you.) Still don't know it. Still can't stop.
My orders say 'none pass'. They don't say I have to stand up.
Sky. Under me, then over me. So that is what the floor of Purgatory is.
(A town under a torn sky. Fires. Something moving in the churchyard, and someone hammering.)
Someone is still here.
Don't stand in the light, lad. They see the light. ...You came down out of it, didn't you.
One hand. A brute took the other. I can still hammer; I can't hold the tongs. You hold, I hit. Deal?
What are we making?
Something that goes down and comes back. Nobody's managed the second part yet.
The sky opened a year ago. First the demons came up out of the churchyard. Then the angels came down. We thought that was help.
It wasn't help. They were gathering. Same as the demons, only cleaner about it.
I was one of them. Half of one.
I know. I've seen the hands. Yours haven't learned to hold yet.
That hook. Give it here.
Thigh bone and a hinge. That hinge is off the church door. I hung that door.
They're not animals, whatever Dace says. Animals don't use hinges.
Forty names on that paper. My wife's is the ninth. 'Called to the Garden early.'
When you get back up there, you tell me what garden.
Hold it steady. Steadier. Right, now don't move.
Good. That's one more they'll have to get through.
Keep your light down when you go in the ground. Both sides can see it.
I've a boy about your age. Had. Go on, I'm busy.
You're not from the sky. The sky ones don't jump, they just come down.
I'm Hanne. I draw what I see so I don't have to keep seeing it.
Want to see the big one's flag? Come back and I'll show you.
Here. It's not a picture. It's just lines.
(A tally mark. Four strokes and a fifth across.)
Where did you see this?
On the ones that climb. They cut it into themselves.
They say the Lowest says it means 'I'm still counting'.
That's the same lines. On your wooden coin. Did you cut them in yourself?
No. Someone counted me.
Then he's down there. The one who counts. Say hello from the drawing girl.
Don't go near the churchyard. That's where they come up. I drew it. It's a bad one.
Pell says you're going down. Will you look at everything? I can't see down from here.
I counted the angels this morning. Nine. Yesterday it was eleven. Where do they go?
Halt. ...Halt doesn't work on your kind, does it. Fine.
Corporal Dace, Third Company. What's left of it.
Where's the rest?
In the ground. Some of them walking about in it.
Clock face. Church tower. Found it in a demon's pack. Don't know why it wanted it.
It's the only thing I've seen one of them carry that it didn't eat. Take it. Find out.
(A brass clock face with no hands. Four shapes are punched around the rim, where the hands would be pinned.)
You read Thorne's letter. He never sent it. I kept meaning to.
He's down there now. If you meet a lad in a red scarf, he was mine. Don't tell him I said so.
Barricade's holding. Barricade's always holding, until it isn't.
They don't rush. They climb a bit, look at us, climb back. Like they're waiting for an order.
Clock's still ticking somewhere. I hear it at night. Nobody else does.
A church is where you go when you want to be heard. I stopped coming for that.
I stopped praying when I understood who was listening.
Who?
Someone who keeps a garden. And weeds it.
The demons shout upward when they climb. Not at us. Past us. A name. Every time the same name.
What name?
I won't say it in a church.
Outside, perhaps. If you come back up.
You've heard it now. It's on your face.
Then I'll say it, church or no. Tobiah. They shout it like a prayer. Perhaps it is one.
The warrant on the door is in the Choir's hand. I used to copy that hand. I taught it.
Pell swears, Dace counts, Hanne draws. I listen. Someone has to.
Go carefully. Below is only above with the lights put out.
Nailed to the church door. 'By the Choir's need, the following are called to the Garden early.'
Forty names. The ink is fresh.
Called early. Mereth was 'not ripe'. They're harvesting.
Demon-made, from a thigh bone and a hinge. The hinge is from a church door.
They came up with tools. Someone taught them.
Never sent. 'Mother, they say the ones in the ground were people once. I don't believe it. I don't want to.'
The churchyard. A hole, and warm air coming up out of it. Like a kitchen.
(From far below, faint: 'Up! He said up!')
Down, then.
You left your other half on the table in there.
Keep it.
We will. We keep everything.
Ungathered. You were seen at the Making. You will be finished.
You dropped my brother.
I have dropped many. I remember none of them. That is a mercy they give us.
The gate... does not open from this side.
I know. I'm not opening it.
(The Warden of the Low Gate lies still. Below the ledge, the gate waits for wings.)
A flat stone with eleven strokes scratched into it. The twelfth is half cut.
Somebody small was counting too.
'What is pressed is not lost. What is lost was never pressed. Sing it until it is true.'
Until it is true. They know it isn't.
Stiff with something that is not blood. The fingers are worn smooth on the inside, where they hold a head still.
They held mine. Halfway.
